nodes.label: BattWatch (Android battery monitor app)
nodes.author: Al-Mothafar Al-Hasan
nodes.rationale: Formerly Simple Battery Notifier. Exists because users get caught out by a dying phone; deliberately positioned against heavy 'power saver' apps, which the author argues Android does not actually need.

nodes.label: GNU General Public License v3.0
nodes.author: Free Software Foundation, Inc.
nodes.rationale: Chosen so the app stays free software: users may use, study, modify and share it including commercially, but any distributed derivative must also be GPLv3 with source available. Closed-source forks are excluded by design.

nodes.rationale: Announcement channel is user-selectable — Toast by default because it is low-clutter, with Notification or None as alternatives.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline
nodes.rationale: Runs tests, builds debug and release APKs, and uploads artifacts on every PR and push to master; it decides nothing about publishing, which stays manual.

nodes.label: User-entered design capacity
nodes.rationale: Android does not expose state-of-health to a normal app, so the user supplies the nameplate design capacity and the app derives a measured health estimate from it.

nodes.label: Distribution channels (Google Play primary, F-Droid planned, self-build)
nodes.norm_label: distribution channels (google play primary, f-droid planned, self-build)
nodes.rationale: Google Play is the primary channel; F-Droid is planned and tracked in issue #4; building from source is always available because the app is GPLv3.

nodes.label: Full charge notification
nodes.rationale: Aimed at users who charge in Airplane Mode for faster charging and would otherwise forget the phone is offline and unattended.

nodes.label: Persistent status notification and per-1%-drop alerts
nodes.norm_label: persistent status notification and per-1%-drop alerts

nodes.label: Quiet hours / customizable notification timing
nodes.rationale: Lets the user suppress alerts while sleeping, so a low-battery warning at 3am does not train the user to mute the app entirely.

nodes.label: Focused unit-test suite (JUnit, Robolectric, Mockito)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately focused rather than exhaustive: covers only the logic most likely to regress — battery math, quiet-hours windows, temperature conversion/hysteresis, and capacity estimation.

nodes.label: Play Store asset directory (play/)
nodes.rationale: Graphics are versioned in the repo so the source of truth lives with the code, but they are uploaded manually in the Play Console — CI neither builds nor publishes them.

nodes.label: In-app launcher icon (mipmap-* / adaptive mipmap-anydpi-v26)
nodes.rationale: Ships inside the APK and is separate from the store icon, but deliberately shares the same BattWatch artwork so the listing and the home screen match.

nodes.label: Conventional Commit PR titles (Copilot rule)
nodes.rationale: PRs are squash-merged so the PR title becomes the commit on master, and that is the text release-please reads to compute the version bump. A CI check enforces the format because a malformed title would silently break versioning.

nodes.label: Versioning rule: never hand-edit the version
nodes.norm_label: versioning rule: never hand-edit the version
nodes.rationale: The version lives only in .release-please-manifest.json and app/build.gradle derives both versionName and versionCode from it (MAJOR*100000 + MINOR*1000 + PATCH), so the two can never drift apart and no commit hash leaks into a version.

nodes.label: Copyleft obligation
nodes.rationale: Anyone who conveys the program or a derivative must pass on the same freedoms they received, which is what prevents a downstream party from taking the work proprietary.

nodes.label: Dual guidelines editions (human-facing vs machine-facing)
nodes.rationale: CODE_REVIEW_GUIDELINES.md is written for human contributors and reviewers; .claude/guidelines.md is the same standards imported by CLAUDE.md so they load into every AI agent session. The two must be kept in sync when a standard changes.

nodes.label: Lightweight, no-bloat design principle
nodes.rationale: No unnecessary background services and no bloated power-saver features, so monitoring never becomes the thing that drains the battery or slows the phone. Trade-off accepted: fewer features in exchange for negligible resource usage.
